aad.name: Aad
aad.title: Aad
aad.dict: An ancient Arabian people, tall and strong, builders of monuments, "Iram of the pillars" (89:6-8). They reject their messenger Hud and are destroyed by a wind that rages seven nights and eight days (69:6-7). Unknown to the Bible.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.title: Aaron (Harun)
aaron.dict: Brother of Moses, given to him as a helper because he is the better speaker (20:29-36, 28:34). In the Quran he does not make the calf: he warns the people against it, and the Samiri makes it (20:85-97). Mary is addressed as "sister of Aaron" (19:28).

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.title: Abraham (Ibrahim)
abraham.dict: Called God's friend (4:125) and the model of pure faith in one God: "neither a Jew nor a Christian" but one who submitted (3:67). He reasons from the star, the moon and the sun to their Maker (6:74-79), breaks his people's idols and is saved from the fire (21:51-70), and breaks with his father. Angels bring him news of a son. He settles some of his offspring by the Sacred House and raises its foundations with Ishmael (2:125-129, 14:35-41). He sees in a dream that he is sacrificing his son, who is ransomed (37:100-111).

abu-lahab.name: Abu Lahab
abu-lahab.title: Abu Lahab
abu-lahab.dict: "Father of Flame": condemned, with his wife, in surah 111. By tradition he was an uncle of Muhammad and one of his fiercest opponents at Mecca. He is the only one of the Prophet's opponents the Quran names.

adam.name: Adam
adam.title: Adam
adam.dict: The first human being, made from clay. God teaches him the names of all things and tells the angels to bow down to him; Iblis refuses (2:30-34). Adam and his wife eat from the forbidden tree, are sent down from the Garden, and are forgiven when Adam "received words from his Lord" (2:37). His wife is not named. The story is told seven times, most fully in 7:11-25 and 20:115-123.

angels.name: The angels
angels.title: The angels
angels.dict: God's servants and messengers, with two, three and four wings (35:1), who do what they are commanded (66:6). They bow to Adam, bring revelation, record each person's deeds (82:10-12), take souls at death (32:11), bear the Throne (40:7, 69:17), and keep Hell (74:30-31). The Meccans called them God's daughters; the Quran calls that a lie (43:19).

azar.name: Azar
azar.title: Azar
azar.dict: Abraham's father, named once (6:74), an idol-worshiper whom Abraham tries to turn and at last disowns (19:41-48, 9:114). The Bible calls Abraham's father Terah.
